newsitem.title: MEXICO: BASEBALL-NICARAGUA DENIED ENTRY INTO CARIBBEAN SERIES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-NICARAGUA DENIED ENTRY INTO CARIBBEAN SERIES.

text.p: Nicaragua won informal membership in the Caribbean Series of baseball on Sunday but not the full acceptance it was seeking in order to play in the annual international competition.

Nicaragua wants to join the Caribbean Series, a tournament of the professional winter league champions from Mexico, Venezuela, Puerto Rico and the Dominican Republic concluding its 27th edition in the northern Mexican city of Hermosillo.
Officials of the Nicaraguan Baseball Federation also said they would like to bring in Cuba as a sixth member nation.

Directors of the Caribbean Professional Baseball Confederation, which runs the series, decided on Sunday to admit Nicaragua as an informal member of the confederation, but without a vote, for two years.
In the meantime, officials said, the confederation will draw up rules for any new country that wants to join the Series.

"We have decided to elaborate regulations that will be more explicit regarding the entrance of new members to the Caribbean confederation," Juan Francisco Puello Herrera, president of the Caribbean Professional Baseball Confederation, told reporters.
"They will be sent to the Nicaraguan league and other leagues that have shown interest," Puello said.
He said a copy also would be sent to Cuba, which has not asked to join.
Baseball is the national pastime in Nicaragua, a poor Central American country, but the level of play there is considered inferior to that of the other Caribbean Series member nations.
Cuba would be more competititve but it is unclear whether the Communist-ruled nation would allow its players to compete in a professional tournament.
